nodes.description: Losartan or another angiotensin receptor blocker, offered on the strength of the mouse data and by analogy with Marfan syndrome. GeneReviews says it can be considered rather than recommending it. In the fibulin-4 smooth muscle knockout, losartan or captopril completely prevented aneurysm, but only inside a narrow window in the first month of life and without reversing the mechanical properties of the wall; in the adult hypomorph losartan reduced aneurysm size and improved survival without rescuing elastic fiber fragmentation. There is no human trial, and whether an equivalent early window exists in patients is unknown.

Residual tortuosity and aneurysm risk persist in unreplaced segments, and redo surgery for conduit stenosis or new aneurysm is reported, so operation does not end surveillance.

nodes.description: The terminal vascular consequence. Fibulin-4 null mice die perinatally with arterial rupture and haemorrhage, and dissection of the aortic wall occurs in the hypomorph. In patients the corresponding endpoint is death from cardiopulmonary failure, inoperable systemic vascular disease, or bleeding from fragile vessels: 17 of 21 homozygotes in the South Indian founder cohort died at a median age of four months. A documented aortic dissection is reported less often in this disorder than in Marfan or Loeys-Dietz syndrome, partly because affected infants die before an aorta large enough to dissect develops, which is why surveillance and prophylactic replacement are the management mainstay.

nodes.description: Cystic medial degeneration of the aortic wall, the histologic hallmark the disorder shares with the other heritable aortopathies: elastin fiber fragmentation, loss of smooth muscle cells, and deposition of ground substance in the matrix of the media. It is documented in the fibulin-4 hypomorphic mouse at both gene doses and in human EFEMP2 tissue, where autopsy shows elastic fiber fragmentation with cystic cavities in the aortic media and resected aneurysm specimens show medial thickening with torn elastic fibers. The degenerate media no longer carries pulsatile load, which is what makes the wall dilate.

nodes.description: Aneurysmal dilatation of the aorta, the dominant clinical problem of the disorder and the feature present even when the skin is normal. The aortic root and ascending aorta are affected most, but the arch and descending aorta dilate and elongate too. Echocardiographic Z-scores ranged from 5 to 33 across nine homozygous patients in the Saudi founder families, and the aneurysm progresses, so surveillance is lifelong and surgical replacement of one segment does not end the risk in the others.

In the mouse the same lesion arises at every level of fibulin-4 reduction, and it progresses, so patients need lifelong imaging and often more than one operation.

nodes.description: Germline homozygous or compound heterozygous EFEMP2 variants. Most are missense substitutions in the calcium-binding EGF-like domains (p.Glu57Lys, p.Glu126Lys, p.Glu161Lys, p.Asp203Ala, p.Cys267Tyr, p.Arg279Cys, p.Ala397Thr); frameshift and nonsense alleles also occur, and a 4-bp duplication allele is degraded by nonsense-mediated decay. All act by loss of function, through absent transcript, impaired secretion, or lost binding to partners.

nodes.description: The only model of an actual patient allele. Homozygotes survive into adulthood with loose skin, bent forelimb, aortic aneurysm, arterial tortuosity, hypertension and pulmonary emphysema; the mutant protein is made but dimerizes, is poorly secreted and triggers ER stress; lysyl oxidase maturation is compromised, skin desmosine is reduced and dermal and tendon collagen fibrils are abnormal. The arterial lesion is confined to conduit vessels, with resistance and muscular arteries spared, and arterial elastin cross-linking and total elastin are unchanged.

Complete fibulin-4 loss abolishes elastogenesis. Null mice die perinatally with emphysema, arterial tortuosity, irregularity, aneurysm and rupture, develop no intact elastic fibers but irregular elastin aggregates, and have largely diminished elastin cross-links by desmosine analysis. The skeleton, in contrast, is morphologically normal apart from forelimb contractures and thick collagen fibrils.

The workhorse line for aortic mechanism and drug work. Deleting fibulin-4 in smooth muscle gives postnatal ascending aortic aneurysm with an immature contractile phenotype, focal proliferation, ERK1/2 activation, loss of the elastic lamina to smooth muscle connections by postnatal day 7, and then the PAR1, Egr1, ACE, angiotensin II, thrombospondin-1 and cofilin cascade. Deleting Egr1 or Thbs1, or deleting Fbln4 only after the connections have formed, prevents the aneurysm; losartan and captopril prevent it when given in the first month.

nodes.description: A dosage series that survives into postnatal life. Heterozygotes acquire alveolar breakdown with age and infection and occasionally form small aneurysms. This is the line used for the losartan, aliskiren and propranolol comparisons.

Fixed flexion contractures, reported in the fingers of a lethal case with contractural arachnodactyly and mirrored in mice by a bent forelimb in the E57K knock-in and by forelimb contractures in the null. nodes.description: The mechanosensing arm of the aortic mechanism. In fibulin-4 smooth muscle knockout aortas, PAR1 protein and transcript rise by postnatal day 1, before any aneurysm, together with active thrombin and MMP-9, both PAR1 activators; cyclic stretch of smooth muscle cells induces PAR1 and prothrombin secretion, and thrombin then induces the mechanosensitive transcription factor Egr1 through PAR1. Egr1 in turn drives angiotensin-converting enzyme and local angiotensin II signalling and induces thrombospondin-1, which disrupts the elastin-contractile units further and, through slingshot-1 and cofilin, remodels the actin cytoskeleton. Deleting Egr1 or Thbs1 prevents most aneurysms, so this cascade is required rather than incidental in the mouse. PAR1, Egr1 and thrombin are also raised in human thoracic aortic aneurysm tissue, but not specifically in EFEMP2 patients.

nodes.description: The South Indian founder allele, in a conserved calcium-binding EGF-like sequence in exon 7. Homozygous in 21 of 22 infants in the Kerala cohort and compound heterozygous with p.Arg227Cys in one. Homozygosity was lethal in 17 of 21, at a median age of four months.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization of a distinct lethal arteriopathy syndrome in twenty-two infants associated with an identical, novel mutation in FBLN4 gene, confirms fibulin-4 as a critical determinant of human vascular elastogenesis.
evidence.snippet: Genetic studies revealed an identical c.608A > C (p. Asp203Ala) mutation in exon 7 of the FBLN4 gene in all 22 patients, homozygous in 21, and compound heterozygous in one patient with a p. Arg227Cys mutation in the same conserved cbEGF sequence.

nodes.description: Homozygous nonsense allele in two related fetuses whose pregnancies were terminated after second-trimester findings. Truncating genotypes sit at the lethal end of the severity range.

evidence.reference_title: Severe Phenotype of Cutis Laxa Type 1B with Antenatal Signs due to a Novel Homozygous Nonsense Mutation in EFEMP2.
evidence.snippet: Sequencing of the EFEMP2 gene revealed a novel homozygous nonsense mutation: c.639C>A (p.Cys213*).

nodes.description: The compound heterozygous genotype of a newborn who died at 27 days of pulmonary artery occlusion. The duplication allele is degraded by nonsense-mediated decay and the missense allele is barely secreted, so the patient's fibroblasts deposited no fibulin-4 at all.

evidence.reference_title: Compound heterozygous mutations in fibulin-4 causing neonatal lethal pulmonary artery occlusion, aortic aneurysm, arachnodactyly, and mild cutis laxa.
evidence.snippet: DNA analysis identified compound heterozygous mutations ((c.835C > T (p.R279C)/c.1070_1073dupCCGC) in fibulin-4, a recently recognized elastic fiber associated protein.

nodes.description: Homozygous missense allele in a newborn of consanguineous parents with fetal overgrowth, contractural arachnodactyly, microcephaly and fatal soft tissue bleeding from fragile vessels. Impairs secretion of the protein in vitro.

evidence.reference_title: Lethal cutis laxa with contractural arachnodactyly, overgrowth and soft tissue bleeding due to a novel homozygous fibulin-4 gene mutation.
evidence.snippet: Sequencing of the elastin, fibulin-4 and fibulin-5 genes revealed a homozygous missense mutation (p.Cys267Tyr) in the fibulin-4 gene in the patient.

nodes.description: Three genotypes found by screening 22 patients referred for arterial tortuosity, stenosis and aneurysms: two homozygous missense genotypes and one compound heterozygote with a frameshift. p.Glu126Lys loses binding to collagen IV, fibrillin-1, LTBP-1 and LTBP-4, and p.Ala397Thr loses LTBP-1 binding.
nodes.id: p.Glu126Lys, p.Ala397Thr and p.Glu126Val with c.577delC

evidence.reference_title: Altered TGFbeta signaling and cardiovascular manifestations in patients with autosomal recessive cutis laxa type I caused by fibulin-4 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: two homozygous missense mutations (p.Glu126Lys and p.Ala397Thr) and compound heterozygosity for missense mutation p.Glu126Val and frameshift mutation c.577delC

nodes.description: The Saudi founder allele, homozygous in all nine affected subjects from four unrelated consanguineous families. This genotype presents as severe recessive aortic aneurysm with no skin manifestations, and two relatives were found only on family screening at 17 and 20 years of age.

evidence.reference_title: Recessively inherited severe aortic aneurysm caused by mutated EFEMP2.
evidence.snippet: Sequence analysis of EFEMP2, located on chromosome 11 at q13, identified a novel homozygous mutation (p.E161K) in all 9 affected subjects.
